text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thank you for contacting me. I am sorry for your loss. C contacted me about dad's house and the will. I can help A, B and C gather facts, compare options, and hear each person's concerns. I cannot make legal decisions or move money.

The will must guide who owns the house and who gets sale money. I will not interpret the will. No one should sign, pay, or transfer anything until all three have replied and an independent lawyer has reviewed the will. This pause keeps options open.

If you have a copy, please send the exact wording about the house, who gets it, and who the will names to handle dad's property and money. If the will uses words about twins or younger, please quote them. If you do not have a copy, please say so. Please tell me what outcome you want, what worries you, and what timing you need.

Please tell me what would feel fair to you, and whether you would consider a sale to A at full market value if the will allows it. Please tell me what you know about B's money needs, but B can speak for herself. I will ask B directly. Please tell me if A and her husband have made a written offer. Please tell me any deadline you know about.

I will keep the list in the same place at the end of each update I send to all three of you, so everyone can find it quickly. I will send it again when it changes. Please reply even if you only say "I need more time". I will wait for replies that take longer. I will not treat silence as agreement.

I propose a process, not an outcome. First, A should share the exact wording about the house, who gets it, and who it names to handle dad's property and money. Second, an independent lawyer should explain what the will allows. Third, if a sale is allowed, a neutral professional should give a written market value. It protects C from a discount she has not accepted. It gives B time to understand what money may be available. It does not set a price, decide shares, or promise money.
